title: createAsyncThunk
description: Learn how to handle async logic with createAsyncThunk and manage loading states.

data.text: **createAsyncThunk** simplifies async operations in Redux by generating three lifecycle actions: `pending`, `fulfilled`, and `rejected`. You write the async logic once, and Redux Toolkit handles the action dispatching automatically.

A thunk is a function that delays an action until later. `createAsyncThunk` wraps your async logic (like a `fetch` call) and automatically dispatches lifecycle actions so your UI can respond to loading, success, and error states without you managing the boilerplate.

data.text: Handling Lifecycle Actions in a Slice

The lifecycle actions are `fetchUsers/pending`, `fetchUsers/fulfilled`, and `fetchUsers/rejected`. You handle them in `extraReducers` using the `builder` pattern. This keeps your async state management predictable and organized.

sequenceDiagram
    participant UI as UI Component
    participant Store as Redux Store
    participant Thunk as createAsyncThunk
    participant API as API Server
    UI->>Store: dispatch(fetchUsers())
    Store->>Thunk: execute thunk
    Thunk->>Store: dispatch pending
    Store->>UI: state updated (loading)
    Thunk->>API: fetch request
    API-->>Thunk: response data
    Thunk->>Store: dispatch fulfilled
    Store->>UI: state updated (data)
    Note over Thunk,API: On error: dispatch rejected
data.caption: Sequence diagram of createAsyncThunk lifecycle

data.text: `rejectWithValue` lets you pass a custom payload to the `rejected` action. Without it, the rejected action's payload would be `undefined`. This is critical for displaying meaningful error messages in your UI.

data.title: Status Pattern
data.text: Use the status string pattern 'idle' | 'loading' | 'succeeded' | 'failed' consistently across slices. It makes your UI logic predictable and your components easy to read.

The second argument to the thunk creator is a 'thunk API' object. It contains `dispatch`, `getState`, `extra`, and `rejectWithValue`. You can also pass extra arguments to all thunks by configuring the store.

data.text: You can abort a thunk using `AbortSignal`. Pass a signal to the fetch call and dispatch an action when the component unmounts or the user navigates away. This prevents state updates on unmounted components.

data.text: Thunks are dispatched just like regular actions. The only difference is that they return a promise, so you can `await` them or chain `.then()` / `.catch()` for imperative logic like showing a toast notification.
